question: What is the primary purpose of applying skull traction?

options.A: To increase blood flow to the brain
options.B: To lower intracranial pressure in head trauma
options.C: To prevent pressure ulcers on the occipital region
options.D: To align and stabilize cervical spine injuries

explanation: Skull traction pulls directly on the skull to straighten and steady broken or dislocated neck bones. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h1)

question: How does skull traction protect the spinal cord from further harm?

options.A: By numbing nerve pathways to block pain signals to the brain
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for future spinal surgery
options.C: By stopping muscle spasms and restoring proper bone alignment
options.D: By increasing cerebrospinal fluid production around the injury

explanation: Pulling forces counteract tight neck muscles that pull bones out of place, keeping the spinal cord safe from pinching. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h1)

question: A patient with which condition is most likely to need skull traction?
explanation: Skull traction is specifically designed for injuries located in the neck portion of the vertebral column. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why is skull traction applied before some neck surgeries?

options.A: To shrink swollen soft tissues around the wound
options.B: To clear bacterial infections from the spinal canal
options.C: To test if the patient is allergic to metal pins
options.D: To realign displaced bones into the correct position

explanation: Pre-operative traction pulls the spine straight so the surgeon has a better starting point for fusion. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h2)

question: Which skull traction device uses spring-loaded pins to monitor safe pressure?
explanation: Gardner-Wells tongs have an indicator to show when the correct tightening pressure has been reached. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of the halo vest over traditional tongs?

options.A: It completely eliminates the risk of pin site infection
options.B: It does not require any pins to penetrate the skin
options.C: It requires no special nursing assessments after placement
options.D: It allows the patient to get out of bed and walk around

explanation: The body jacket secures the ring, permitting mobility unlike bed-bound tong setups. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h3)

question: What equipment must be kept at the bedside before applying skull traction?
explanation: Respiratory compromise can happen suddenly during cervical manipulation, requiring emergency airway support. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why is baseline neurological assessment important before skull traction starts?

options.A: To detect any changes in nerve function after the procedure begins
options.B: To prove the patient is mentally competent to sign financial forms
options.C: To determine if the patient requires general anesthesia in the theatre
options.D: To calculate the exact amount of weight needed for the pulley system

explanation: Knowing the patient's starting neurology helps nurses quickly identify if spinal alignment affects nerve pathways. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h4)

question: Where must traction weights be positioned at all times?

options.A: Supported by a small stool placed under the bed
options.B: Tied tightly to the headboard of the hospital bed
options.C: Resting securely on the bottom mattress frame
options.D: Hanging freely without touching the floor or bed

explanation: Weights must hang completely free so the correct pulling force is continuously maintained. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the main role of the nurse while the doctor places skull tongs?

options.A: Drilling the small pilot holes into the patient's outer skull
options.B: Holding the head in neutral alignment to prevent movement
options.C: Administering general anesthesia through an intravenous line
options.D: Tightening the pin screws to the manufacturer pressure limit

explanation: Maintaining a steady, straight head position protects the damaged spine while the device is secured. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h5)

question: How often should neurovascular checks be performed on a patient in skull traction?

options.A: Only when the patient complains of pain
options.C: Every fifteen minutes for the first week
options.D: Once a day during morning care

explanation: Frequent checks catch early signs of nerve compression or poor circulation in the limbs. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h6)

question: What should a nurse do if a traction rope slips out of the pulley groove?

options.A: Lift the patient's head off the bed to relieve the tension
options.B: Realign the rope in the pulley without changing the weight position
options.C: Tighten the skull pins further to make up for the lost force
options.D: Remove all the weights permanently until the doctor arrives

explanation: Fixing the mechanical setup keeps the therapeutic pull steady and prevents sudden jolts to the neck. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h6)

question: What solution is commonly used to clean skull traction pin sites?

options.A: Warm soapy tap water and vinegar

explanation: Gentle antiseptic or saline cleanses the area without damaging healing skin tissue around the pins. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h7)

question: Which finding at a pin site requires immediate reporting to the doctor?

options.A: Firm skin tightly surrounding the pin
options.B: A small amount of clear dried serum
options.D: Absence of pain around the metal site

explanation: Pus and heat are classic signs of localized infection that could spread to the bone. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the FIRST action a nurse must take if a skull traction pin detaches?

options.A: Remove the remaining three pins to keep the skull balanced
options.B: Lower the head of the bed flat to rest the patient
options.C: Manually stabilize the head and neck in neutral alignment
options.D: Run to the nurses station to find the attending surgeon

explanation: Protecting the cervical spine from sudden movement takes priority when mechanical traction fails. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h8)

question: Which complication is most critical to monitor for in high cervical spine injuries?

options.A: Inability to move the lower legs only
options.C: High fever due to a urinary infection

explanation: Injuries high up in the neck can paralyze breathing muscles, making airway compromise an emergency. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h8)
